title: Build an App With Claude Design
format_note: On-camera designer narrates a screen-recorded walkthrough; the presenter footage and the title sit on a canvas with the product's own selection handles and toolbars.
one_thing: Claude Design lets you ask for options, comment and edit them, get a click-through prototype, then tell Claude to build it.

transcript.voice_style: Casual first-person presenter, conversational and unscripted in tone, with small jokes about a silly side project.
transcript.script_shape: Anecdote about a silly app (0-17s), self-intro, the problem (onboarding), five numbered steps with two coffee breaks, then 'Not bad', 'build it', and a one-line invitation.

structure.frame0: Presenter video in a framed box with a filename label 'Claude-Design-Demo.mov', selection handles and a cursor on a light dotted canvas; subject present, not black (f0001.jpg).
structure.first_3s: Presenter talks to camera while the box grows from small to 750 px wide and gains selection handles at t=0.67s; cursor drifts away (strips/window-01-0s.jpg).

beats.what: Presenter pitches a dumb daily-challenge app inside a canvas frame.
Frame slides up; green title card appears, recolours to lavender via a swatch click.
Phone artboard shows 'Draw a picture', edited down to 'Dra', then 'Upload bird noises'.
Presenter introduces himself; a typed comment card reads 'Hi, I'm Nate. I'm a designer at Anthropic.'
Presenter fills the frame and explains the onboarding problem.
Blur-through into the Claude app: pick folder, Artifacts, Design, type the prompt.
Coffee-break gag: portrait clip of presenter drinking from a mug, with a toolbar coffee button.
Chat plus canvas show five onboarding artboards; comment card 'Bigger bird. Much bigger.'
Inline text edit 'Bet you won't.', properties panel with radius field.
Burst of seven cuts: reply, prompt typing, second coffee clip, Click-through artboard, Play.
Full-screen prototype: bird, time picker, CAW counter; prompt 'ok claude. build it.'
Presenter in a shrinking frame says 'And that's it' and closes.
Serif line 'Claude makes it.' is typed, selected, trimmed to 'it.' and fades.
Claude starburst logo and wordmark on cream.

hero_moment.what: Five generated onboarding artboards (yellow, blue bird, cream terms, navy wheel) appear beside the current screen after the coffee gag (f0030.jpg).

ending.what: Typed tagline resolves to the Claude logo; the spoken CTA is 'try collabing with Claude on it' at 1:34.

rhythm.how_change_is_paced: Long presenter shots (longest 19.75s, 19.3% of runtime) carry typed comment cards; screen demos cut every 1-3s; one burst of 7 cuts in 7.3s at 72-79% of runtime (metrics.json bursts).

on_screen_lines.text: How an Anthropic designer uses Claude Design
Hi, I'm Nate. I'm a designer at Anthropic.
design a silly onboarding for this silly app. start from what we have currently, and do a series of designs for new ideas
Bigger bird. Much bigger. It should be uncomfortable.
You're in. Go make bird noises.

copy.holds_vs_reading_rule: The title card holds about 4.8s against 2.6s needed for 7 words and the logo holds 2.2s; 'Claude makes it.' holds about 1.5s against a 1.4s need. Product text is shown only as long as the action takes.

sound.music: Music tagged 0.682 alongside speech 0.680; keyboard_musical 0.449 and synthesizer 0.413 suggest a soft keys/synth bed; percussion 0.342, drum 0.269. About 103 BPM, beat confidence 0.236, so a faint pulse only.
sound.sfx: Nothing in audio.json identifies sfx; I could not hear it.
sound.vo_music_balance: Presenter speech is the main track from 0 to about 95s; sections A-E change at 4.7, 19.9, 54.2, 95.6s, the last one under the ending.
sound.energy_arc: Flat and quiet: LRA 2.6 LU, short-term max -22.5 LUFS; no silence spans. The only structural change is the outro section at 95.6s.
sound.sync_to_picture: Cuts are not locked to the sound: 0.13 of cuts land on strong onsets against 0.137 chance. Picture follows the spoken steps instead, e.g. prompt typing at 52s with narration at 0:53.

good.observation: The product's own editing chrome (selection handles, toolbars, comment card, cursor) frames the presenter and the title, so the film demonstrates the tool before it explains it.
Typed on-screen text changes meaning on screen: 'Draw a picture' is cut to 'Dra' and becomes 'Upload bird noises', showing the premise in one gesture.
Every step of the workflow is shown as the real action in the real app: folder pick, Artifacts, Design mode, prompt, five artboards, comment, edit, prototype, build.
Both coffee waits are a 2s joke clip, so 'I go get a coffee' compresses the AI wait without a time-lapse.
The prototype screens are large, high contrast and legible: 'Today you may only make bird noises.', time picker, CAW counter.
The ending uses the idea of the film: the tagline is typed in an editor, selected, trimmed to 'it.', then replaced by the logo.

weak.observation: Chat panes, sidebar and properties panel are small text; the tiny artboard copy at 21-28% canvas zoom would not read at phone width.
The loudness is -24.5 LUFS with true peak -7 dB, about 10 LU under a -14 LUFS social master.
The first 40s are presenter-led and the product appears only at 40.7s; the hook is a joke idea rather than the product.
Cuts are not locked to the music (0.13 against 0.137 chance), and the music is near-inaudible in measured loudness range of 2.6 LU.

rule_candidates.rule: Show the real product doing each step, ideally 45% or more of runtime, and keep each screen only as long as its action takes.
rule_candidates.evidence: 48% of runtime is real Claude app capture, 40.7-89.8s; median shot 2.31s.

rule_candidates.rule: Frame on-camera or hero footage as an object on the product's canvas, with a filename label, selection handles and cursor, so the UI chrome carries the transitions.
A single long presenter shot can run about 20s if a typed card or text change updates every 2-4s; the 1.8-3.5s cut cadence applies to shots with nothing else changing.
rule_candidates.evidence: Longest shot 9.38-29.12s (19.75s, 19.3% of runtime); comment card text changes at 16-22s.

rule_candidates.rule: Place the burst of cuts when the narration lists steps, not at 30-60%; here 7 cuts in 7.3s start at 72% and lead into the prototype payoff.
Type the exact prompt on screen as the line is spoken, and punch in 2x on the input box so the words read.
rule_candidates.evidence: Prompt typed 50-54s (f0025-f0027), spoken 'Design a silly onboarding' at 0:53.

rule_candidates.rule: Two-line title with one bold accent phrase at 6-8% of frame height: 57px of 720 for line 1 and 4 words max a line.
rule_candidates.evidence: Title card at t=6: lines 57px (7.9%) and 44px (6.1%), accent 'Claude Design'.

rule_candidates.rule: End on a typed or edited tagline that resolves to the logo and hold the logo 2s or more.
When speech carries the film, music can sit very low, but measure it: this master is -24.5 LUFS, 10.5 LU below the -14 LUFS target.
rule_candidates.evidence: metrics.json sound: -24.5 LUFS, true peak -7 dB, LRA 2.6 LU.
